Also that women love dick. Even more than I love tacos...

When you're in love, you want to put your partner before yourself. However, your partner may not want to put you first and thus you must tread carefully.

Source: I was the one who put myself first and I left my partner in ruins
I put her before me, and she left me in ruins after i had a year long struggle with depression and anxiety...
That if you truly love someone, you have to consider if they'd be better off without you in their life, and maybe let them go.
I say this for anyone you care about. We as people try to fight and hold on to things way to much and end up making it harder or braking what we are trying to hold on to.
that my definition of "first relationship" changed over time. That first relationship wasn't really a relationship as much as infatuation and immaturity on my part.
That 16 year old me, was willing to fake it in order to prolong something that wasn't working, because they didn't want to be alone.

This. Now that I have proven to myself I can get/sustain a girlfriend, I don't need to date people I necessarily don't like. I been alone for several years because I haven't really hung out with someone that I feel would make a good fit.
That the problem with dating someone who is infatuated with you in the hope they'll get bored and leave you alone, is that they don't.

That people can use it to manipulate you if you aren't careful, so obviously the only thing to do is to close yourself off from everyone ever because love isn't meant for you.

That no, she wasn't the girl of your dreams. You will be fine.

What you THINK you need is not what you actually need. Unfortunately, the only way to discover what you really need you have to put yourself in front of the person you THINK you need and let him/her club you repeatedly on the head until you get the message. Yes, it's complicated.

Reciprocated love is a naturally-occurring (metaphorical) drug that will lead you into doing inadvisable things. It will get you very high. The withdrawal symptoms are unpleasant. I also know, from experience, that this advice will almost never be followed by anyone until they have tried it themselves, and that's probably as it should be. Following the relationship, I also learned I no longer felt any need to be romantically loved by another person to be happy or complete - after a brief period, nothing felt missing from my life. This is a very useful way to be.

Edit: words
Not to let someone get full controll over me.
That love doesn't mean that things will work out no matter what. Life isn't a Disney movie and it takes more than just emotion to make it work.
That whatever happens in a relationship, there's always something good you can take away from it in the end and carry into future relationships or just your own life.

That a lot of early relationships start not because the people are in love, but because they just want someone to make them feel loved.

It's important to protect yourself and take care of yourself, they might not be with you forever but you will be there for yourself always.
